summary: One decompression/expansion step of a bit-expansion state machine. When the state byte at this+9 equals 16, deinterleaves the input buffer a2 by factor 2 (copying every second byte), packs the samples contiguously, then advances the state: sets state to 8, output stride (this+11) to 8 times the source stride (this+10), and element count (this+4) to count times source stride. Returns the state object pointer.

local_names.a1: expansion state object: count at +0, count at +4, state byte at +9, source stride byte at +10, output stride byte at +11

operations.description: Test state byte at this+9 equals 16; when not equal, skip the whole body and return the state object unchanged.
Compute element count = dword at this+0 times the source-stride byte at this+10; if zero, skip the copy loop.
Deinterleave: copy every second byte from the input buffer into a contiguous output region, count elements times.
Advance state fields: set state byte at this+9 to 8, output-stride byte at this+11 to 8 times the source-stride byte, and dword at this+4 to count times source stride.
Return the state object pointer a1.

unresolved: Meaning of the state enum (16 -> 8) and of the stride fields at +10/+11 is derived from the state machine but not externally confirmed.
Whether a2 is overwritten in place or must alias separate regions is unknown.
